newsitem.title: USA: United Illuminating sees '97 revenues down.
newsitem.headline: United Illuminating sees '97 revenues down.

text.p: The United Illuminating Co said on Monday it expected its 1997 retail revenues to be below those of 1996.

The company said in a statement that the drop would be caused by an order from Connecticut's Department of Public Utility Control mandating that United Illuminating reduce rates and undertake conservation measures.
The utility reported 1996 retail revenues of $650 million against $639 million the year before. Total revenues in 1996 were $726 million, against $690 million in 1995.

Because of the order, United Illuminating would have an allowed annual return on equity of 11.5 percent between 1997 and 2001, a cut of nearly one percent from the previously allowed return of 12.4 percent. The reduction in return is equivalent to about $0.30 a share.

"Income earned from higher sales or reduced expenses that produces a return above the 11.5 percent return level will be shared by one-third being applied to customer bill reductions, one-third applied to more rapid amortization of assets and one-third retained by shareholder," also by order of the Connecticut department, the statement said.
A cut of about $15 million will be due to reduction in customer bills directly ordered by the department.
The company said it expected 1997 sales to rise about one percent from 1996, adding about $6 million to sales margin.
Long-term contracts with major customers "also are expected to lead to reductions in retail revenues that have averaged $2 million to $3 million per year in the recent past."
